I think about this year the same way I thought about last year. My land is small — only 1.8 mu — so I cannot waste money, but I also cannot afford a bad harvest. Five mouths to feed.

My main rotation is wheat then maize, like everyone around me in Quzhou. I keep a small strip of cotton because my mother-in-law always grew it and the price has been okay. But most of the land is wheat-maize.

For wheat, I sow in October. I buy the improved seed from the town dealer — the same one my neighbor Li uses, because her wheat stood well last year and did not fall over in the rain. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (about 40 kg, the 15-15-15 kind) before ploughing, and then I topdress urea at jointing — maybe half a bag. The well is close, so I irrigate 3 times: after sowing if the soil is dry, at jointing, and at grain-filling. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2 times. I expect around 450 kg from each mu — that is what I got last year.

For summer maize after wheat, I use hybrid seed — "Zhengdan" or whatever the dealer pushes, neighbors get the same. I do not plough, just plant straight into the wheat stubble because I have no time between harvests. I put compound fertilizer in the row at sowing, then urea once when the plants are knee-high. Irrigate 2 times if the rain does not come. Spray once for borer. I hope for 550 kg per mu.

For cotton on the small strip (0.3 mu), I plough properly. Cotton needs more care — more fertilizer, more spraying, maybe 4-5 times for bollworm. But only a tiny piece so the cost is not too big.

I would rather put a little extra urea than have yellow leaves. Fertilizer money is real, but a bad harvest is worse.
